clue.text: Seem almost gloomy, but open to being placated

indicators.note: almost says the word for seem stops one letter short of its end

parts.note: to seem is to appear
sable means black, dark or gloomy, chiefly in poetry and heraldry

explanation.surface: Someone looking downcast may nonetheless be ready to be won round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' cuts the last letter off APPEAR, leaving APPEA.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who can be pacified or soothed is ready to be calmed by concessions.

clue.text: Cooler shade it provided for Wordsworth's youth

definitions.meaning: cooler is slang for a jail

definitions.text: shade it provided for Wordsworth's youth
definitions.meaning: Wordsworth's Immortality Ode says shades of a jail begin to close upon the growing boy

explanation.surface: A remark about a cool shady spot that sheltered the young poet.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ode line reads 'Shades of the prison-house begin to close / Upon the growing Boy'.
explanation.definitionFit: A cooler is slang for a jail, the building where convicts are held.

clue.text: Wild flower, say, with name in Latin and English

parts.note: EG, for example, means say

indicators.note: in says the letter for name goes inside the word Latin

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A wild flower described in two languages.
explanation.definitionFit: Eglantine is sweetbriar, a wild rose of hedgerows.

clue.text: Partly reveals how Bizet is used in entertainment industry

indicators.note: Partly says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Music critics show how a composer's work is put to use by the entertainment world.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition took in 'is used in', which are link words: the answer means the entertainment industry alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Showbiz is informal for show business, the world of popular entertainment.

clue.text: Overnight stay in base with crack fleet

parts.note: a bed is a base or foundation, as in a bed of concrete
and means with or plus
to break is to crack
fleet means fast or swift

explanation.surface: Naval jargon about a quick fleet resting at base.
explanation.definitionFit: This is lodging for a night with a morning meal, a guest-house stay.

clue.text: Executed attractive print

indicators.note: executed means beheaded, so the word loses its first letter

parts.note: fetching means attractive

explanation.surface: A nice print has been well done.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Executed' looks like 'carried out'; here it means beheaded, removing the F of FETCHING.
explanation.definitionFit: An etching is a print made from an acid-bitten metal plate.

clue.text: Request to be on time for work

indicators.note: in a down-or-across charade, one piece being on another means it follows it, so the request comes after the time

parts.note: to request is to ask

explanation.surface: Someone is asked to turn up punctually for their job.
explanation.definitionFit: A piece of work set for someone is a job or assignment.

clue.text: Strange story in a northern setting

indicators.note: a setting surrounds a jewel, so the letters for a northern hold the story

parts.note: a story is a lie, a fib

explanation.surface: A tale set somewhere in the North.
explanation.definitionFit: Alien means foreign or unfamiliar, hence odd.

clue.text: New approach, leading with King or Jack

indicators.note: leading with says the king's letter comes first, before the others

parts.note: K is the chess and card abbreviation for king
Ave, short for avenue, is an approach to a building

explanation.surface: A card player tries a new line, opening with a king or a jack.
explanation.definitionFit: In cards the jack is also called the knave.

clue.text: Bonnie's youthful state

parts.note: Bonnie read as a typical girl's name: her young days are the time when she was a lass rather than a woman

explanation.surface: A remark about the early years of someone called Bonnie.
explanation.definitionFit: The period of being a young female, before womanhood, is a youthful condition.

clue.text: Get into trouble taking a glass of wine

parts.note: to cop it is British slang for to be punished or get into trouble

explanation.surface: Someone lands in hot water for sneaking a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: COP IT is everyday British slang for getting into trouble or being punished.
explanation.definitionFit: A copita is a tulip-shaped Spanish glass used for sherry, so the word names a glass of wine.

clue.text: Wealthy man following Henry — he died to mix socially

indicators.note: following says the wealthy man's word comes after the pieces for Henry and he died

parts.note: H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance
OB, short for Latin obiit, means he died and appears on gravestones
a nob is a rich or upper-class person in British slang

explanation.surface: An obituary-like line about a rich man coming after a dead Henry, oddly ending in socialising.
explanation.walkthrough: OB (obiit, Latin for 'he died') is a crossword staple from tombstones; NOB is British slang for a toff.
explanation.definitionFit: To hobnob is to mingle familiarly with others, especially those of higher status.

clue.text: Something offensive in use can get thrown out

indicators.note: letters that get thrown out are scattered and so rearranged here

explanation.surface: Something unpleasant in a bin is chucked away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get thrown out' rearranges the letters of IN USE CAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A nuisance is an annoyance; in law it is something that harms or offends neighbours.

clue.text: Device the church eliminated from birth control

indicators.note: eliminated from says the church's letters are removed from the longer word

parts.note: contraception is birth control
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: The church has struck contraception from its teaching.
explanation.walkthrough: CE (Church of England) taken out of CONTRACEPTION.
explanation.definitionFit: A contraption is a gadget or machine, often makeshift.

clue.text: Asian connection, so to speak

indicators.note: so to speak means the word for connection is said aloud rather than spelt

parts.note: a tie is a bond or connection

explanation.surface: Someone describes an Asian link in loose terms.
explanation.definitionFit: A person from Thailand is an Asian by nationality.

clue.text: Shoot big game in backward eastern state — it's cooked with wine

indicators.note: in says the hunting words sit inside the letters for the state and eastern
backward says the abbreviation for the state is read from right to left

parts.note: AZ is the postal abbreviation for Arizona
to bag game is to shoot or kill it
the lion is the classic big-game animal

explanation.surface: A hunting trip in some backwater state, oddly followed by a recipe.
explanation.walkthrough: AZ is the US postal code for Arizona; 'backward' turns the whole 'eastern state' run, and 'in' sets the hunting words inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Zabaglione is an Italian dessert of egg yolks and sugar whisked with Marsala, a fortified wine.

clue.text: Popular form of art leading to strange rowdiness

indicators.note: leading to says the earlier pieces come before the word for strange

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
Deco, short for Art Deco, is a style of art
rum is British slang for odd or strange

explanation.surface: A trendy art movement ends in a weird riot.
explanation.walkthrough: RUM is old British slang for odd.
explanation.definitionFit: Indecorum is improper or unseemly behaviour, a lack of decorum.

clue.text: An extra good queen filled with new majesty

parts.note: a super, short for supernumerary, is an extra in a film or play

indicators.note: filled with says the letter for new is placed inside the queen's name

parts.note: Good Queen Bess was the popular name for Elizabeth I

explanation.surface: Someone calls a queen fresh and outstanding, praising her grandeur.
explanation.walkthrough: 'An extra good' looks like one phrase meaning 'very good'; it splits into a film extra and Good Queen Bess, the nickname of Elizabeth I.
explanation.definitionFit: Majesty is grandeur or magnificence, a state of being splendid.

clue.text: Almost lose blood, wave as means of alerting doctor

indicators.note: Almost says each of the two words loses its final letter

parts.note: to bleed is to lose blood
a perm is a hair wave

explanation.surface: A patient near bleeding to death signals for a doctor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' trims both BLEED and PERM: BLEE + PER.
explanation.definitionFit: A bleeper is a pager that beeps to summon a doctor.

clue.text: It interrupts flow of air, producing sore lip, possibly

indicators.note: possibly says the letters could be rearranged into another word

explanation.surface: A cold wind gives someone a sore lip.
explanation.definitionFit: A spoiler on a car or wing disrupts the airflow to cut lift.

clue.text: Fish with John in boat

definitions.meaning: the John ... is a sea fish, so this word goes with John to name it

explanation.surface: A fisherman called John sits in his boat with his catch.
explanation.definitionFit: The name is both half of a fish's name and a kind of small fishing vessel.

clue.text: Delivery that may get round a striker

definitions.text: Delivery that may get round a striker

parts.words: Delivery that may get round a striker
parts.note: in cricket, a bowled ball that spins from the leg side past the batsman's bat; the surface suggests delivering a letter past a picket

explanation.surface: A post delivery that dodges a worker on strike.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a delivery is a bowled ball and the striker is the batsman facing it.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket this spinning ball turns from leg to off, so it can beat the batsman's bat.

clue.text: Healthy litter unsettled, initially, by their accommodation?

indicators.note: initially picks the opening letters of the two words before it

parts.note: a sty is where a litter of pigs lives

explanation.surface: A litter of piglets is disturbed by their pen.
explanation.definitionFit: Lusty means vigorous and strong.

clue.text: Seize key file

parts.note: G is a musical key
a rasp is a coarse file

explanation.surface: Grab the key to the file.
explanation.definitionFit: To grasp is to grip firmly.

clue.text: Hold attention of tenant

definitions.meaning: to keep them busy or absorbed
to tenant a building is to live in it as a tenant

explanation.surface: A landlord keeps a lodger's attention.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb covers both keeping someone engaged and living in a property.

clue.text: One drink put in another, regardless of expense

indicators.note: put in says the first drink goes inside the second

parts.note: to sup is to drink
to lap is to drink as a cat does

explanation.surface: A cocktail made by pouring one drink into another, never mind the cost.
explanation.definitionFit: A slap-up meal is lavish and lavishly spent on, with no thought for cost.

clue.text: Every bit of work. I note, is causing bad reaction

parts.note: every bit of something is all of it
the erg is the unit of work in physics
C is a musical note

explanation.surface: Someone remarks that the whole job is making them ill.
explanation.definitionFit: Something hypersensitive in effect triggers an immune response, a bad bodily reaction.

clue.text: Off-putting affliction

parts.note: read as affecting one's putting: the golfing nerves that make a player twitch on the green

explanation.surface: A complaint that repels people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Off-putting' looks like 'unpleasant'; it means spoiling a golfer's putting.
explanation.definitionFit: In golf this is a nervous twitch that wrecks short putts.

clue.text: Work stoppage disrupts entire term

indicators.note: disrupts says these letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A strike breaks up the whole school term.
explanation.definitionFit: Retiring from one's career means stopping work for good.
